summary: Validate data at the boundary and keep the trusted core typed.
principle: Parse untrusted input in one place and pass typed values inward.
whyItMatters: A typed function cannot see a malformed payload that never passed the parser.
whenToApply: HTTP handlers, hook payloads, config files, and model output.
whenNotToApply: A pure function that already receives a value checked by its caller.
commonFailureModes: Casting JSON with as
Catching a parse error and continuing with a partial object
verificationSteps: Send one invalid field and confirm the caller rejects it
evidenceNeeded: The parse call and the failure path
tradeoffs: A schema is more code than a cast
example: A hook body is parsed before any field is stored.

summary: A process on the request path must not wait on slow work.
principle: Return quickly from a hook and do heavy work after the user is unblocked.
whyItMatters: A slow hook holds the coding agent even when the advice is optional.
whenToApply: Editor hooks and request handlers that only observe.
whenNotToApply: An explicit user command that the user is waiting on.
commonFailureModes: Network call inside the hook
Scanning the whole repo before returning
verificationSteps: Confirm failure still returns a success response
evidenceNeeded: Hook source and its timeout behavior
tradeoffs: The first panel update can be incomplete
example: Prompt capture writes one log line and prints continue true.

summary: Changing a response shape is a compatibility break unless clients were written for it.
principle: Add fields in a compatible way and version or feature-flag a breaking change.
whyItMatters: Existing callers keep compiling or parsing against the old contract.
whenToApply: Any payload another service or browser already reads.
whenNotToApply: A brand-new route with no callers.
commonFailureModes: Renaming a JSON field
Reusing 200 for a new error
verificationSteps: Compare the old and new example bodies
tradeoffs: Keeping the old field costs a little clutter
example: A new optional field is added beside the old one.

summary: A retried write needs an idempotency key or a natural unique constraint.
principle: Accept a client key and treat a repeat as the same operation.
whyItMatters: Timeouts cause clients to retry a request that already landed.
whenToApply: Creates that charge, enqueue, or insert.
commonFailureModes: Two rows for one user click
A unique error that the client treats as failure after success
tradeoffs: The server must store keys for a retention window
example: The second POST with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original result.

summary: A query filter should be able to use an index.
principle: Match the leading index fields to the filter and sort you actually run.
whyItMatters: A collection scan gets slower as the data grows and can time out a request.
whenToApply: New find or aggregate filters on a non-trivial collection.
commonFailureModes: A leading wildcard regex
A filter that skips the index prefix
verificationSteps: Check explain or the index list for those fields
tradeoffs: Extra indexes slow writes and use disk
example: find({ tenantId, status }) uses a compound index starting with tenantId.

summary: A write the user must not lose needs an explicit durability choice.
principle: Know whether the write is acknowledged by a majority before you tell the user it succeeded.
whyItMatters: A primary can acknowledge and then fail over before a secondary has the write.
whenToApply: Money, auth, and other records the product treats as committed.
whenNotToApply: A cache or a log line that can be dropped.
commonFailureModes: Default write concern left unread
A retry that duplicates a non-idempotent insert
evidenceNeeded: Client options or a comment that names the concern
example: The insert awaits majority acknowledgment before the response is 201.

summary: Two writes that must succeed together belong in one transaction.
principle: Commit related row changes in a single transaction and name the isolation you need.
whyItMatters: A crash between two statements leaves a state no invariant allows.
whenToApply: Transfers, migrations that backfill, and multi-table updates.
commonFailureModes: Autocommit between debit and credit
A migration that locks a hot table with no rollback note
evidenceNeeded: The begin/commit or the query runner
example: Both ledger rows commit or both roll back.

summary: A migration that old code still runs against should expand before it contracts.
principle: Add the new shape, deploy code that writes both, then remove the old shape.
whyItMatters: A drop-column migration deployed before the new code crashes the previous version.
whenNotToApply: A database nobody else is connected to.
commonFailureModes: Renaming a column in one step
A NOT NULL column without a backfill
verificationSteps: Check the previous app version still boots
example: The new column is nullable until backfill finishes.

summary: At-least-once delivery means the consumer must tolerate duplicates.
principle: Make the handler idempotent and bound the retry with a timeout and a dead-letter path.
whyItMatters: A timeout after a successful side effect delivers the same message again.
whenToApply: Any consumer that writes, charges, or sends.
whenNotToApply: A pure projection that can be rebuilt from scratch.
commonFailureModes: No dedupe key
Retries with no delay
A poison message that blocks the queue
verificationSteps: Read the timeout and dead-letter settings
example: A second delivery of the same message id no-ops.

summary: The visibility timeout must be longer than the work, or another worker will double-process.
principle: Set the lock or visibility window above the worst-case handler time and extend it if work runs long.
whyItMatters: A second worker starts while the first is still writing.
whenNotToApply: In-process async work with no competing consumer.
commonFailureModes: Default timeout left at 30 seconds for a multi-minute job
verificationSteps: Compare timeout to the slowest external call
tradeoffs: A long timeout delays retry of a crashed worker
example: The handler heartbeats the visibility timeout while it waits on a partner.

summary: Every state-changing path needs an explicit authorization check.
principle: Authenticate the caller and authorize the action on the specific object.
whyItMatters: A valid login is not permission to read or change someone else's record.
whenToApply: Routes and jobs that accept an id.
whenNotToApply: A public health check with no data.
commonFailureModes: Checking the role and skipping object ownership
Trusting a client-sent user id
verificationSteps: Call the path as a different user
evidenceNeeded: The check and the object lookup
example: The order id is loaded and compared to the session tenant before update.

summary: Secrets do not belong in source, logs, or client state.
principle: Load secrets from a secret store and redact them before logging.
whyItMatters: A key in a task history or webview is a credential leak.
commonFailureModes: Key in settings.json
Token echoed in an error string
verificationSteps: Search logs and webview messages for the key prefix
evidenceNeeded: The storage API used for the key
tradeoffs: Secret storage is less convenient than a config file
example: The provider key stays in the extension host secret store.

summary: Money is an integer in minor units plus a currency.
principle: Store amounts as integers in the currency's minor unit and keep the currency on the record.
whyItMatters: Binary floating point cannot represent every decimal amount.
whenNotToApply: A display string that is not stored as the source of truth.
commonFailureModes: number of rupees in a float
Mixing paise and rupees in one field
verificationSteps: Check a 0.1-style case is an integer count of minor units
evidenceNeeded: Schema or type of the amount field
example: 1099 and USD mean 10.99 dollars, not 1099 dollars.

summary: A capture or payout retry must not move money twice.
principle: Key the ledger post by a stable operation id and ignore a duplicate.
whyItMatters: A retried payout is a second transfer if the first one already settled.
whenNotToApply: A quote that does not post.
commonFailureModes: New idempotency key on every retry
Recording success before the provider ack
tradeoffs: The key store must outlive the retry window
example: The second attempt returns the original payout id.

summary: A test status is real only when the command result was observed.
principle: Record pass or fail from an exit code or reporter you saw, and otherwise say not observed.
whyItMatters: An agent sentence that says tests passed is a claim, not evidence.
whenNotToApply: A docs-only change where you explicitly skip tests.
commonFailureModes: Marking passed because the agent said so
Treating a missing command as a failure
tradeoffs: The panel will often say not observed
example: npm test with no parsed exit code stays not observed.

summary: A useful test fails when the behavior breaks, including one failure path.
principle: Cover the behavior you changed and at least one way it can fail.
whyItMatters: A test that only asserts a happy mock does not catch the regression.
commonFailureModes: Asserting the mock was called and nothing else
No test for the empty or error input
evidenceNeeded: Test name and the branch it hits
tradeoffs: More tests take time to read
example: The parser test includes one rejected payload.

summary: Interactive controls need an accessible name and a visible focus state.
principle: Use a real button or link, give it an accessible name, and do not remove focus outlines without a replacement.
whyItMatters: Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot operate an unlabeled div.
commonFailureModes: Click handler on a div
Outline removed with no :focus-visible style
verificationSteps: Confirm each control has a name
example: The quiet-mode control is a button named Toggle quiet mode.

summary: Motion should honor the user preference to reduce it.
principle: Disable non-essential animation when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
whyItMatters: Animation can make a tool unusable for some people.
commonFailureModes: Infinite pulse with no media query
verificationSteps: Check the stylesheet for the media query
example: The status chip does not pulse when reduced motion is requested.
